constraint: WebRTC ICE candidates must agree with the claimed network position and must not reveal a host address inconsistent with it.

notes: Jointly owned by subsystems 9 and 10. UNENFORCED, and what it needs. The candidate list is already measured - the collector's webrtc.ice probe records every candidate with its address class and port class - so the missing half is entirely the network: (1) an egress at the claimed position, i.e. a real proxy or VPN exit whose IP geolocates where the profile says the user is, (2) a STUN or TURN server reachable THROUGH that egress, since a srflx candidate is what carries the exit address into the candidate list at all, and (3) a geolocation reference for the exit IP to compare the claim against, which is a database rather than a measurement. Without (1) the probe records candidates for the host's real network and the check would compare a claim against the wrong network - passing or failing for a reason that has nothing to do with the browser. Jointly owned with subsystem 10, and the egress is the blocker.

constraint: Against an origin advertising HTTP/3, the browser must attempt QUIC wherever stock Chrome would, including when a proxy is configured.

evidence.note: QUIC is attempted only when proxy_info_.is_direct(), so a proxied session silently loses HTTP/3

notes: Why SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE is a coherence requirement rather than a feature. See docs/subsystems/network-proxy.md. UNENFORCED, and what it needs: three pieces of network infrastructure and one observation channel. (1) An origin advertising HTTP/3 - Alt-Svc h3 or an HTTPS RR - either ours or a pinned public one, because the statement is conditioned on the advertisement. (2) A SOCKS5 relay that implements UDP ASSOCIATE, since the point of the row is that a proxied session must not silently lose h3. (3) Two runs against that origin, one direct and one proxied, which is the comparison the statement makes. The observation channel is the part no page can supply: PerformanceResourceTiming.nextHopProtocol reports the protocol that was USED, so a run that attempted QUIC and fell back to h2 is indistinguishable from one that never attempted it. The attempt is only visible in a net-log (--log-net-log) as QUIC_SESSION creation against that origin. So the enforcer is a two-run net-log harness, not a check over a capture, and it is one test away rather than one infrastructure project away: the relay is the only piece we do not already have.

constraint: A profile should claim resources at or below what the host can satisfy. Claiming more is permitted but carries weak-evidence risk, because measured parallelism plateaus at the host's real capacity.

evidence.note: thread pools size from NumberOfProcessors, so a worker scaling curve plateaus at the host's real core count whatever the reported value says

notes: Weak, not fatal. A scaling-curve probe fires on containerized, virtualized, loaded and throttled real browsers alike, so no detector can rule on it. The loader clamps and warns rather than refusing: trading a rarely-probed weak signal for a hard usability failure is the worse deal. Only two fields are host-coupled; device identity is portable. WHY THIS EDGE AND coh.claim-within-host-capacity POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, recorded once so neither reads as a relaxation of the other: memory and core count are CLAMPED to the host because the user cannot install RAM to make a claim true, so an unbacked claim is falsifiable by allocation. Fonts are ASSUMED because the user can install them, so the honest move is to tell them to. The distinguishing factor is whether the user can change the host, not how loud the tell is. Owner directive and CdpSurface's phrasing, this session.

constraint: A session configured through a proxy must remain proxied across network changes. No transport may reconnect directly to the origin.

evidence.note: Migrate() reconnects to connection()->peer_address(), so a peer address set to the origin rather than the SOCKS relay would open a direct socket to the origin on every network change

notes: Not a fingerprinting edge but a leak: the failure is silent, only occurs on network transition, and deproxies the session including the real client address. Settled in docs/subsystems/network-proxy.md by requiring the QUIC peer address to be the relay. UNENFORCED, and what it needs, which is genuinely more than a test. Beyond the h3 origin and the SOCKS5 relay that coh.quic-attempted-when-offered needs, it needs (1) a network change the host can force mid-session while a QUIC session is live - two real interfaces, or the interface the session is bound to going down and up, because Chromium's migration path is driven by the network change notifier and not by anything a page can trigger - and (2) proof of where the sockets went AFTER the migration. A net-log showing QUIC_SESSION_MIGRATION plus the peer address is suggestive but not decisive, because the failure is a socket opened to the origin rather than a session state: the decisive observation is a packet capture on the host showing no UDP datagram addressed to the origin's address for the lifetime of the session. That means root, a capture interface and a deterministic way to induce the transition, which is why this one is an infrastructure project: the check is easy and the instrument is not. It is also the only row in this group whose failure is a leak of the real client address rather than a fingerprint.

notes: Recorded as an edge specifically because sample count is one of the few render inputs we can legitimately set, and the temptation when setting it is to change the report without changing the allocation. Doing that turns a valid configuration change into a detectable one. Patch 0119 serves the anchor's MAX_SAMPLES to WebGL on every backend, so on an M4 Max under a Windows NVIDIA anchor MAX_SAMPLES reports 8 while the device has 4. That does not break this edge, because MAX_SAMPLES is a ceiling and not the drawing buffer's configuration: DrawingBuffer takes min(preference, MAX_SAMPLES) with a preference of 4, so the buffer is allocated at 4 and SAMPLES, SAMPLE_BUFFERS and the rendered coverage all agree with each other. The anchor itself measured MAX_SAMPLES 8 beside antialiasSamples 4, so the served pair is the pair a real machine reports. What a page can still see is the ceiling itself: renderbufferStorageMultisample at 8 is refused on a 4-sample device, which is a probe on the limit rather than a disagreement between the report and the render.
